extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants (PD/PI and senior/key_personnel) preparing Senior/Key Person Profiles, biographical sketches, and Facilities & Other Resources sections
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and examples for completing the Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded), the NIH Biographical Sketch (A–D), and the Facilities & Other Resources / Major Equipment descriptions for a grant application. Includes required fields, page limits, and exemplar content showing how to present personnel qualifications and available resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch — format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH. Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biosketch must follow the prescribed A–D format (Personal Statement; Positions and Honors; Contributions to Science; Additional Information: Research Support and/or Scholastic Performance) and must be limited to five pages per person. Include identifying information (name, position title, education/training table). Attach the biographical sketch file when submitting (PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement: a concise narrative describing the individual's overall research goals, current research program, relevance to the proposed project, and justification of the person's suitability to lead or participate in the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Personal Statement should highlight expertise, experience, and demonstrated record of successful and productive research relevant to the application (for example: statement of overall goal, current focus, collaborations, and how the PI's expertise prepares them to lead the proposed experiments). May include key accomplishments and how they support the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: List of academic and professional positions held and honors/awards received (chronological entries such as Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor, and named awards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dates and institutional affiliations. Also list significant professional memberships and service (e.g., editorial boards, study section service, conference leadership) that demonstrate standing in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbered summaries of up to several major contributions to science, each with a brief explanatory paragraph and selected representative citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each contribution describe the scientific advance and its significance, and supply key publications (with citations and PMCID/PMID where appropriate) demonstrating the contribution. Use multiple subitems (a., b., c., …) to give representative works for each described contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Additional Information: Research Support and/or Scholastic Performance
rubrics_metrics.description: A listing of 'Ongoing' and 'Completed' external support entries with grant numbers, dates, project titles/major goals, and the individual's role (e.g., PI, co-I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report active and pending support and past support relevant to the investigator's track record. For each entry include project period, major goal/aim, role, and note overlap (e.g., 'No overlap with current proposal' where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profile — required fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) form requires identification and contact fields: Prefix, First/Middle/Last Name, Suffix, eRA Commons user name (credential), Position/Title, Organization Name, Department/Division, Address, Phone, E-Mail, Credential (agency login), Project Role (e.g., PD/PI), Degree Type, Degree Year, Attach Biographical Sketch (file), Attach Current & Pending Support (file), Tracking Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all required fields as indicated (asterisked). Provide attachments for biographical sketch and current & pending support. Use accurate project role designations (PD/PI, co-investigator, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — comprehensive description of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional and laboratory resources available to support the project, including equipment, core facilities, biosafety level labs, instrumentation, computational resources, reagents/collections, and physical spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detail on instruments (make/model where relevant), counts/quantities, BSL levels (e.g., BSL2, BSL3, ABSL4), specialized facilities (cold rooms, dark rooms), and access arrangements (on-site, core facilities). Highlight unique capabilities (e.g., automated stainers, confocal microscopes, FACSAria flow cytometer, Illumina MiSeq) and any institutional computing/network capacity. Examples in the document enumerate many items to illustrate the expected level of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major Equipment — list and quantify major instrumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: List major equipment in the laboratory and adjacent equipment suites, including ultracentrifuges, centrifuges, incubators, biosafety cabinets, microscopes, freezers (–80°C, –20°C), PCR units, plate readers, rotavaps, hydrogenators, NMR, HPLC/MS, GPU/CPU computational servers, and other large instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific models/numbers when possible (e.g., '2 Beckman L90 ultracentrifuges', 'Nikon Ti Eclipse confocal microscope system (1)') and indicate quantity. This supports reviewers' assessment of whether the environment is adequate and whether required equipment access is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagents and specialized collections as resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Document on-site availability of reagent collections and specialized libraries (e.g., '>30,000 members including >1,000 boronic acids, bar-coded, searchable electronic database').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate size, special indexing (bar-coded/searchable), and accessibility to project personnel to demonstrate resource sufficiency for the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational resources and software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe computational infrastructure (network bandwidth, workstations, servers with GPUs/CPUs, RAM and storage) and key software suites available (e.g., Schrodinger’s Small Molecule Drug Discovery Suite, GROMACS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify hardware configurations (cores, RAM, GPUs, SSDs) and essential software/licenses. This allows reviewers to judge computational feasibility for computational chemistry, modeling, or bioinformatics aims.
